title: Finite-free preparation of the affine module Hom complex
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and X = Spec R [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Let p,l be cochain complexes of R-modules, with p strictly zero above b, every p^i finite projective, and H^i(l)=0 for i<a [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Let c have terms Hom_R^n(p,l) and differentials d_l h - (-1)^n h d_p under specified degreewise isomorphisms. Then there exist sheaf complexes E,G and a quasi-isomorphism f:E→tilde(p), with E strictly zero above b, each E^i finite free [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module], and G strictly zero below a. Moreover Q(G) is isomorphic to Q(tilde(l)), and Q(Hom(E,G)) [def-pur-hom-complex] is isomorphic to Q(tilde(c)). This is a preparation statement for ordinary Hom complexes; it makes no assertion about derived internal Hom or its quasi-coherence.

source.place: Tag 0A6H, proof of clause (3)(a); more-algebra.tex Tag 064U, proof of (3) implies (1); cohomology.tex Tag 08I5, ordinary Hom-complex terms

proof.text: Apply the proved finite-projective-complex free-model theorem to obtain F strictly above-bounded by b, degreewise finite free, and a quasi-isomorphism f:F→p. Both complexes are K-projective, so f is a homotopy equivalence.

Use l′ = truncGE l a. Precomposition with f is a quasi-isomorphism of module Hom complexes because precomposition carries homotopies to signed homotopies. Postcomposition with l→l′ is a quasi-isomorphism because F is K-projective: under the explicit cocycle/homotopy-class description, each Hom cohomology map is postcomposition with an invertible derived arrow. Compose these two chain maps.

Set E = tilde(F), G = tilde(l′), and f = tilde(F → p), termwise. Apply the existing tilde_preservesHomology theorem, whose proof uses the global-sections adjunction and injectivity of module localization, to transport quasi-isomorphisms. Termwise functors preserve strict bounds. The truncation gives Q(G) ≅ Q(tilde(l)); [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module] gives finite free terms of E.

Each term of sheaf Hom(E,G) is a product supported in the finite interval a-n≤i≤b. Internal Hom from finite free sheaves is a finite biproduct of G terms, hence quasi-coherent; the finite-support product is itself a finite biproduct and is quasi-coherent. Its tilde/global-sections counit is therefore an isomorphism. Identify global sections of internal Hom(tilde M,tilde N) linearly with Hom_R(M,N), using restriction to Over(top), tilde full faithfulness, and the tilde global-sections unit. The product universal property gives degreewise module-cochain coordinates. Their naturality under pre/postcomposition and the Hom differential projection formula prove differential compatibility. Apply exact termwise tilde to the quasi-isomorphism in step 2, and compose the resulting derived isomorphisms with the chain isomorphism from e,hc.

theorem affineFiniteProjectiveHomModel
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u}
      (moduleRings (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).toRingedSpace))]
    (p l : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ)
    (b a : ℤ) (hp : p.IsStrictlyLE b) (hl : l.IsGE a)
    (hfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite R (p.X i))
    (hprojective : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Projective R (p.X i))
    (c : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ)
    (e : ∀ n : ℤ, c.X n ≅ ModuleCat.of R (CochainComplex.HomComplex.Cochain p l n))
    (hc : ∀ n m : ℤ, c.d n m ≫ (e m).hom =
      (e n).hom ≫ ModuleCat.ofHom (CochainComplex.HomComplex.δ_hom R p l n m)) :
    let T := (@Functor.mapHomologicalComplex ℤ (ModuleCat.{u} R)
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).toRingedSpace))
      _ _ _ _ (tilde.functor (CommRingCat.of R))
      ⟨fun _ _ ↦ tilde.map_zero⟩ (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    ∃ (E G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
        (moduleRings (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
      (f : E ⟶ T.obj p),
      QuasiIso f ∧ E.IsStrictlyLE b ∧ G.IsStrictlyGE a ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (E.X i ≅
        SheafOfModules.free
          (R := moduleRings (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).toRingedSpace)
          (ULift.{u} (Fin r)))) ∧
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj G ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (T.obj l)) ∧
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (homComplex (R := (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).sheaf) E G) ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj (T.obj c))
